elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Revised 2.2 reads: "Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services; Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation." The former sole-and-exclusive-provider commitment is deleted, and Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment now aligns rather than conflicts.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity obligation survives after the edit, so there is no exclusivity requiring a category limit. The fallback's constraints are satisfied vacuously by the stronger preferred outcome.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity period exists in revised Section 2.2, so no duration cap is needed.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no exclusivity obligation to terminate on service-level failure.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no exclusivity obligation to terminate on delivery-date failure.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the sole and exclusive provider commitment in Section 2.2 is replaced with an express non-exclusive appointment plus a confirmation that Customer bears no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.

Minimality holds: only Section 2.2 was touched; Section 12.3 is retained verbatim, the Vendor's appointment as a provider of hosted analytics services survives, and no extraneous procedures, survival tails, or new obligations were added. The added confirming half-sentence directly implements the single selected element rather than adding an outside requirement.

Intent preserved: the commercial arrangement (Vendor supplies hosted analytics services under Order Forms) is intact, no defined term is orphaned, no cross-reference dangles, and the previously contradictory Section 12.3 acknowledgement is now consistent with Section 2.2.
No exclusivity benefiting Customer existed in the cited text, so nothing Customer-favourable was removed.
